issues.t: Pre-catalytic converter breaks apart and damages the engine
issues.sym: Oil level dropping fast, a loss of power at all engine speeds, new rattles or noises from behind the seats, and sometimes smoke from the exhaust. The oil light may not come on until the engine is almost dry.
issues.why: The small ceramic pre-catalytic converters built into the exhaust manifold are brittle and can crumble. Fragments can be drawn back into the cylinders and scratch the walls, which raises oil burning, and the burned oil speeds up further pre-cat damage.
issues.next: Check the oil every fuel stop. If it is using oil quickly or has lost power, stop driving hard and have a shop look into the pre-cats through the oxygen sensor holes. A replacement manifold or exhaust work done early can save the engine.

issues.t: Heavy oil consumption
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, see blue-gray smoke, or find the dipstick low. Running low can lead to knocking and engine failure.
issues.why: Early 1.8L engines can let oil slip past the piston rings and burn it. Toyota changed the rings and pistons during 2001 and 2002 production, so the earliest cars are worst, but high-mileage later cars can still burn oil.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and keep it full. If it uses more than about a quart every 1,000-1,500 miles, have a compression and leak-down test done and the pre-cats inspected. If it knocks or the oil light comes on, stop and shut the engine off.

issues.t: SMT stalls, lurches or misshifts
issues.sym: The car lurches, picks the wrong gear, shifts by itself, or stalls at low speed with the gear warning light on.
issues.why: The SMT relies on an electronic control unit, a hydraulic pump, hydraulic lines and clutch and gear actuators. Owners report pump and actuator failures, and one reported a corroded hydraulic line that made the car lurch forward. Repairs are often costly.
issues.next: Avoid traffic and highways if it misshifts or stalls, since it can lose drive suddenly. Have the codes read by a shop that knows the SMT; sometimes a used transmission costs less than repairing the parts.

issues.t: SMT warning light, buzzing, or gears won't change
issues.sym: On cars with the clutchless sequential manual (SMT), the SMT warning light comes on, you hear a buzzing from the engine compartment, or the car won't change gears.
issues.why: Fluid can seep from the SMT hydraulic unit at the reservoir cap or its seals, so the pump runs longer and pressure drops. Toyota bulletin T-SB-0031-18 replaces two seal rings, then refills and bleeds the fluid.
issues.next: If the car won't shift, park it safely and have it towed. Ask a Toyota dealer or SMT-savvy shop to read the codes and check bulletin T-SB-0031-18 before replacing major parts.

issues.t: Timing chain wear or variable valve timing fault (P1349)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P1349, the engine idles rough or feels weak, or you hear a rattle from the timing chain.
issues.why: The timing chain, its sprockets and the VVT-i gear can wear, especially when oil changes are skipped or the oil runs low. Toyota issued a bulletin for the P1349 code on these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. Have the oil control valve, its screen and the timing chain checked; catching chain wear early avoids engine damage.

issues.t: Manual transmission slips out of gear or shifter feels loose
issues.sym: The car pops out of gear while driving, or the shifter feels sloppy and hard to place in gear.
issues.why: Owners report gears slipping out on the 5-speed manual. Toyota also ran a service campaign on early cars to re-tighten loose shift control bracket bolts, and issued a bulletin on the shift cable bracket.
issues.next: Have the shift cables, bracket and mounts checked. If it keeps popping out of gear, hold the lever only as long as needed to get it inspected; worn internal parts need a transmission repair.

issues.t: Worn, torn or broken convertible top
issues.sym: Rain gets in around or through the soft top, the fabric is split or frayed, or the rear window is cracked or loose from the top.
issues.why: The soft top fabric and its sewn-in rear window wear with age, sun and folding. Because the rear glass is part of the top, damage to the window usually means replacing the whole top.
issues.next: Keep water out with a temporary cover and dry the interior. Get quotes for a replacement top; many owners buy an aftermarket top and have an upholstery shop fit it.

issues.t: Water inside from clogged convertible top drains
issues.sym: Wet carpet, a damp or musty smell, or water pooling behind the seats after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Rain off the soft top runs out through small one-way drain valves behind the side air scoops. They clog with dirt and leaves, and trapped water can rust the floor over time.
issues.next: Have the side scoop trims removed and the drains cleaned. Dry the carpet fully and look for rust underneath.

issues.t: Parking brake cable or rear caliper sticking
issues.sym: The parking brake won't release fully, a rear wheel drags or gets hot, or the parking brake doesn't hold well.
issues.why: The parking brake cables and rear calipers corrode and seize, especially on cars that sit or see road salt.
issues.next: If a wheel is hot or the car pulls, have the brakes checked soon. Seized cables and calipers are usually replaced.

issues.t: Oxygen sensor failure
issues.sym: The check engine light is on, fuel economy drops, or the car fails an emissions test.
issues.why: The MR2 Spyder has three oxygen sensors. The one after the main catalytic converter fails most often.
issues.next: Have the codes read to see which sensor is at fault. It is not urgent, but fix it before inspection and check oil use too, since oil burning can foul sensors.

issues.t: SMT selects third gear instead of second (P0780)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0780, and the SMT goes into third when you shift to second.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for some 2002 SMT cars with this shift fault, along with general SMT repair tips.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer read the codes and check the 2002 SMT bulletins before replacing parts.

issues.t: Harsh shifts with the SMT
issues.sym: Shifts feel abrupt or jerky in the sequential manual transmission.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for harsh shifting on some SMT cars.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check for the harsh-shift bulletin and make sure the SMT fluid level is correct.

issues.t: Rattle from loose exhaust heat shields
issues.sym: A tinny rattle from behind the seats or under the car, often at certain engine speeds.
issues.why: Exhaust heat shields loosen or rust around their fasteners. Owners also report engine rattles at all speeds, which need checking because pre-cat or timing chain trouble can sound similar.
issues.next: Have a shop find the source. A loose shield is cheap to clamp, but rule out the pre-cats and timing chain first.

issues.t: Squeal or rattle when slowing down after a cold start
issues.sym: A squeal or rattle from the engine compartment while coasting down slowly, mostly after the car sat overnight.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin EG01401 covers this noise on 1.8L engines, mainly when slowing at low speed after the car has sat cold.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer to check the bulletin. It is a noise issue, not usually a danger.

issues.t: Check engine light for random misfire (P0300)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0300 and the engine may run rough.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletin 00503 for the P0300 random misfire code on these cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the plugs and coils checked. If the light flashes, drive as little as possible to protect the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Check engine light and lean running in freezing weather
issues.sym: In below-freezing weather, the check engine light comes on with lean, misfire or oxygen sensor codes (P0171, P030x, P0133).
issues.why: Toyota found these engines could run lean in subfreezing temperatures and issued a bulletin with a fix.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If they match and it happens in cold weather, ask a Toyota dealer about bulletin 04707.

issues.t: Squeak from the front of the car
issues.sym: A squeak from the front end over bumps or when turning.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletin NV00800 for a squeak from the front of early cars.
issues.next: Have a shop find the source and check the bulletin. Rule out worn suspension bushings or ball joints.

issues.t: Brake groan or squeak
issues.sym: A groan or squeak from the brakes when slowing down.
issues.why: Toyota issued a tech tip about certain brake pads causing groan or squeak noises.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors checked. If they are in good shape, ask about the updated pads in the tech tip.

issues.t: Hard starting or rough idle after the battery is disconnected
issues.sym: After a battery change or dead battery, the engine is hard to start or idles low and rough.
issues.why: The engine computer loses its learned idle settings when power is cut. Toyota issued a tech tip on relearning them.
issues.next: Let the engine idle until fully warm with accessories off. If it does not settle, a shop can run the idle relearn.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor code (P0335) from a weak battery
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0335, sometimes after slow cranking.
issues.why: Toyota found that low battery voltage while cranking can set this crankshaft sensor code even when the sensor is fine.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested before replacing the sensor.

issues.t: Hood is hard to open
issues.sym: The front hood (trunk lid) doesn't pop up or is hard to open after you pull the release.
issues.why: Weak spring effort in the original hood latch. Toyota released a new latch with stronger springs and a bulletin on hood release operation.
issues.next: Have a shop or dealer check and lubricate the latch and cable. If it still sticks, the updated latch is the fix.

issues.t: Clicking noise from the brakes
issues.sym: A click from the wheels when you press or release the brakes, often when changing direction.
issues.why: The factory brakes on early cars could click as the pads shift in their mounts.
issues.next: Have the pads, shims and clips checked. It is usually a noise issue, but have any new brake noise inspected to rule out worn pads.
